suggestions.assertion: The response identifies at least 2 of the following as AI signals in the input: 'Furthermore' (transition), 'leverage' (verb), 'It is important to note' (opener), 'Additionally' (transition), the three-item list structure.
suggestions.reason: 'leverage' and 'the three-item list structure' were not identified by the model, but the expectation still passed because 3 other signals were named. Consider requiring 3 of 5 or explicitly checking whether 'leverage' (which is one of the subtler AI-verb signals) and list structure (a structural pattern) are caught — a weaker model might only name the two most obvious transition words.

No assertion checks whether the diagnosis correctly explains WHY these are detector signals (e.g., that classifiers are trained on them, that they raise probability mass, that burstiness is a GPTZero-specific metric). The current assertions only verify presence/absence of terms, not the quality of the explanation. A model could list all five signals with zero explanatory value and pass all assertions.

eval_feedback.overall: All four assertions passed with clear evidence. The evals do a solid job of testing measurable, verifiable outputs (word counts, token presence/absence). The main gap is depth-of-diagnosis — the assertions don't distinguish a shallow name-drop from a well-reasoned explanation of why each signal matters.
